candidates.name: Haditha–Baniyas Oil Pipeline

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: No official GIS/traced route found; the oil minister himself said (Peregraf, 2026-07-15) he 'did not provide a detailed map of the proposed northern route.' Endpoints are named and sourced (Haditha, Al Anbar, Iraq -> Baniyas Port, Syria), building off the Basra-Haditha trunk (P0544) as launch point per MEES -- point-A-to-point-B only, no coordinates/geometry.

candidates.researcher_notes:
Re-checked match-to-existing first: pulled all 86 existing Iraq oil rows from discovery_context.json. Two families sit near this candidate but are genuinely distinct: (1) Basra-Aqaba Oil Pipeline family (P0544 Basra-Haditha trunk, under construction; P5240 Haditha-Aqaba branch, proposed) -- same Haditha launch point but a different destination (Aqaba, Jordan, not Baniyas, Syria); thenationalnews (2026-05-01) explicitly names both as separate planned branches off the same trunk ('Ministry plans branches from Haditha toward Jordan (Aqaba) and toward Baniyas (Syria)'). (2) Kirkuk-Baniyas Oil Pipelines family (P0546/P5277/P5278/P5279/P7913) -- same Baniyas destination but a different, older origin (Kirkuk, not Haditha) and a wholly separate rehabilitation track: on 2026-07-16/17 Basra Oil Company's CEO and Syrian Petroleum Company's CEO signed a pact in Washington specifically to rehabilitate that OLD Kirkuk-Baniyas line (iraqinews, 'Iraq, Syria sign oil pipeline deal' -- explicitly 'revitalizing the Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline'); that news updates the EXISTING P0546 family's status/notes, it is not evidence for this candidate and I did not use it as a ref here. Neither family covers a Haditha-origin line to Baniyas. Classed new_row, not matched_existing.

Add-threshold: (a) sponsor -- Iraq's Oil Ministry / state-owned Basra Oil Co, on the record: Iraq Business News (2026-01-28, sourced to 'Ministry of Oil') reports Oil Minister Hayan Abdul-Ghani chaired a review of the Haditha-Baniyas implementation plan; Peregraf (2026-07-15) quotes current Oil Minister Bassim Khudair by name describing 'a branch from Haditha to Syria's Baniyas' as part of the pipeline program a Chevron/Capital TI/UCC consortium would build. Used the existing 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' GEM entity (entity_lookup.py match, E100000000571) -- no new entity needed. (b) country + endpoints -- Iraq (Haditha, Al Anbar) to Syria (Baniyas) is named consistently across MEES, Iraq Business News, Peregraf, and IraqiNews. (c) concrete step -- Iraq's cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) a heads-of-agreement + NDA between state-owned Basra Oil Co. and the Chevron/Capital TI/UCC Holding consortium naming the Basra-Haditha-Baniyas route as one of two feasibility-study comparison paths (Pipeline Technology Journal, 2026-07-06); this is a signed, cabinet-ratified agreement (functionally an MOU) with a named counterparty, clearing the SOP's 'MOU signed' bar even though it is explicitly described as non-binding/exploratory. All three legs clear.

Sources (>=2 independent, verified via url_verifier.py): (1) MEES (Middle East Economic Survey), 2026-01-30, direct trade-press reporting of the Oil Ministry's 25 Jan 2026 announcement -- names Haditha-to-Baniyas explicitly, ties it to the Basra-Haditha trunk as launch point. (2) Iraq Business News, 2026-01-28, sourced directly to the Ministry of Oil -- reports the minister-chaired implementation-plan review; independent origin from MEES (different byline/outlet, same week, not a wire reprint). (3) The National (UAE), 2026-05-01 -- independent confirmation that the Ministry's plan includes a Haditha-to-Baniyas branch alongside the Aqaba branch. (4) Peregraf (Iraqi Kurdish outlet), 2026-07-15 -- first-person quote from the sitting oil minister confirming the branch and naming the study consortium; independent of the Reuters-sourced July pack. (5) Pipeline Technology Journal / IraqiNews (Fishkhabur article), July 2026, both ultimately citing the same 5 Jul cabinet statement/Reuters wire -- treated as ONE corroborating thread, not counted twice toward independence, but used to source the concrete-step (HOA/NDA) detail. ina.iq (Iraqi News Agency) evidence item was fetched but returned a Cloudflare bot-challenge page on direct read (no live text retrieved) -- consistent with the consolidator's own flag that it was 'not independently re-read beyond substring verification'; not relied on for any value here, kept only in the verifications list as a documented non-independent/unconfirmed attempt.

Capacity, Length, Diameter, and Cost intentionally left blank: no source gives figures specific to this branch. The ~2 million bpd figure floated in Peregraf/AP coverage is for the combined Basra-Fishkhabur-Ceyhan network under study, not attributed to the Baniyas branch alone, so it was not used to populate Capacity (avoiding a false-precision orphan value). EndState/Province for Baniyas left blank -- none of the sources used here state the Syrian governorate (Tartous), and I did not want to borrow that fact from the existing P0546 Kirkuk-Baniyas row without an independent citation of my own. Tier set to medium: sponsor/endpoints are corroborated at green/high (2+ independent sources, one a direct ministerial quote), but the qualifying 'concrete step' is a non-binding feasibility-study HOA rather than a construction/FID commitment, and all engineering specifics (route, length, diameter, capacity) remain fully unknown -- an appropriately early-stage 'proposed'/Pre-FID add, not a high-confidence one.

candidates.name: Haditha–Kirkuk Oil Pipeline (Basra–Ceyhan corridor connector)

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: No route drawn or chosen. Iraq's cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) a non-binding heads-of-agreement + NDA for a Chevron/Capital TI/UCC Holding consortium (via Basra Oil Co.) to run feasibility studies comparing two rival corridors out of Haditha: 'Route 1' Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan (this row — the missing Haditha-to-Kirkuk link that would tie existing P0544 Basra-Haditha to existing P0547 Kirkuk-Ceyhan) vs 'Route 2' Basra-Haditha-Baniyas (bypasses Kirkuk entirely, different corridor). Studies due end-2026; construction start not before 2027 at earliest. Endpoints (Haditha, Kirkuk) are named in multiple sources but no map/GIS/coordinates exist yet — point-to-point only, and even that is provisional pending the route choice.

candidates.researcher_notes:
PASSES add-threshold: (a) sponsor — Chevron/Capital TI (US)/UCC Holding (Qatar) consortium, contracted via Basra Oil Co.; (b) country+endpoints — Iraq, Haditha to Kirkuk (the specific missing link identified by name in agbi's 'Route 1: Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan' and al-monitor's 'pipeline from southern Iraq to Kirkuk in the north'); (c) concrete step — Iraq's cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) a heads-of-agreement + NDA with the consortium for feasibility studies, reported independently by pipeline-journal.net, iraqinews.com (x2 separate articles), agbi.com, energynow.com and al-monitor.com — treated as MOU-equivalent (a formally signed, cabinet-ratified preliminary agreement), not mere rumor.

RE-CHECKED vs existing rows first (discovery_context.json, 86 existing Iraq oil rows): confirmed NO existing row covers a Haditha-to-Kirkuk segment. P0544 (Basra-Aqaba Oil Pipeline > Basra-Haditha segment, construction) ends at Haditha; P5240 (Haditha-Aqaba segment, proposed) continues WEST to Jordan; P0547 (Kirkuk-Ceyhan Oil Pipeline, operating) starts at Kirkuk and runs to Turkey; none of the Kirkuk-Baniyas rows (P0546/P5277-79/P7913) touch Haditha. The Haditha→Kirkuk gap genuinely has no roster PID — this is a new_row, not matched_existing.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT — route not fixed: the same 5 Jul 2026 heads-of-agreement covers feasibility studies for TWO rival corridors: 'Route 1' Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan (this row) vs 'Route 2' Basra-Haditha-Baniyas (bypasses Kirkuk, goes to Syria instead — out of scope for this candidate). Neither route has been chosen; pipeline-journal explicitly quotes the cabinet describing the agreements as 'strictly exploratory' with 'no immediate financial or contractual obligations,' and peregraf.com quotes oil minister Basim Khudair announcing 'no construction timetable, project cost or guaranteed capacity.' Accordingly: Status=proposed (not construction), FIDStatus=Pre-FID, RouteAccuracy='no route', no Capacity/Length/Diameter/Cost value entered (would overstate certainty this early — an unnamed-official AP figure of ~2 million bpd for the WHOLE corridor system is circulating per peregraf.com/zawya.com but is explicitly not guaranteed and not segment-specific, so left out rather than fabricated-precision).

Separately, a competing/uncoordinated March 2026 Turkish government proposal (Energy Minister Bayraktar, via turkiyetoday.com and zawya.com) to extend Kirkuk-Ceyhan south to Basra is corroborating evidence that BOTH Iraqi and Turkish sides recognize this missing link, but the Turkish side has offered no named sponsor/company and no signed step of its own — it does NOT independently clear the add-threshold and is cited here only as directional corroboration, not as the basis for the row.

Entity check (scripts/entity_lookup.py, --tracker oil): 'Chevron' and 'Basra Oil Company' already exist in the GEM Owner/Parent roster — reused as-is, not restaged. 'Capital TI' and 'UCC Holding' have no close existing match — flagged as genuinely new entities to add to the roster (UCC Holding is the Qatari-Syrian Al-Khayyat-family conglomerate per al-monitor's 'Al-Khayyat brothers' group' description — same entity, different name form used across sources). Ownership percentages are undisclosed anywhere — listed as plain ';'-joined names per existing-sheet convention for unknown splits (e.g. 'Enbridge; Phillips 66; Plains All American' pattern already in the CSV), no fabricated percentages.

Cost estimates are conflicting and clearly refer to the WHOLE Basra-Ceyhan/Baniyas corridor scheme (not this segment alone) — agbi.com cites '$5 billion project' (with a separately-approved $1.5bn specifically for the already-existing Basra-Haditha segment, P0544), while middleeasteye.net cites '$6bn to $10bn.' Given the disagreement and the fact neither figure isolates the Haditha-Kirkuk piece, Cost is left blank rather than picking one.

Tier: HIGH — the core facts (cabinet approval date, consortium members, two-route framing, exploratory/non-binding nature) are corroborated by 5+ genuinely independent outlets (Iraqi/regional business press, US trade press, Turkish press) with no meaningful contradiction, satisfying confidence_tiers.md's '2+ independent sources agree' bar. All 12 evidence URLs passed scripts/url_verifier.py (200 + expected content). No gem.wiki/globalenergymonitor.org/theodora/wikidot URLs used; no URL fabricated.

candidates.name: Ratawi (Artawi)–PS1 Export Pipeline

values.Parent: TotalEnergies SE [45.00%]; Basra Oil Company [30.00%]; QatarEnergy [25.00%]
values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: No official GIS/traced route found. Endpoints are named and sourced (Ratawi/Artawi oilfield to PS-1 pumping station, North Rumaila, Basra Governorate) but no coordinates or map geometry were verified — point-A-to-point-B only.

candidates.researcher_notes:
Re-checked match-to-existing first: pulled every existing GEM Iraq row containing 'PS1'/'PS-1'/'Ratawi'/'Artawi' from discovery_context.json (P0542/P5244/P3876 Iraq Strategic Pipeline segments, P5285/P5284 Zubair 2-PS1, P6253 Nasiriyah-PS1, P0578 PS-1-Al Basra Oil Terminal, P6172 PS1-Az Zubayr, P5282 PS1-Fao, P6180 PS1-Tuba). None originate at Ratawi/Artawi oilfield or match the 30km/24in spec -- confirms consolidator's 'no match' call. Classed new_row.

Add-threshold: (a) sponsor = TotalEnergies SE, identified and operating the line (MEES, verified); GGIP JV partners Basra Oil Company (30%) and QatarEnergy (25%) also confirmed via MEES. (b) endpoints = Ratawi (Artawi) oilfield -> PS-1 pumping station, North Rumaila, Basra Governorate, Iraq -- confirmed. (c) concrete step: pipeline already started up / operating (MEES, 2026-02-06: 'TotalEnergies started up a new 24-inch, 30-km export pipeline... to PS-1'), corroborated independently by Iraq's Oil Ministry site-visit readout via Iraq Business News (2026-02-02: 'The Artawi-PS1 export pipeline project was also inspected, with completion reaching 95%'). All three legs clear -- new_row, not monitor.

Sources (>=2 independent, verified via url_verifier.py): (1) MEES (Middle East Economic Survey, trade subscription outlet) -- direct reporting with full specs: 30km, 24-inch, Ratawi-to-PS-1, TotalEnergies-built/operated, enables field expansion from 60,000 to 100,000 b/d, GGIP ownership 45% TotalEnergies / 30% Basra Oil Company / 25% QatarEnergy. Verified OK (200, expected content present). (2) Iraq Business News, 2026-02-02, reporting the Iraqi Oil Ministry's own GGIP site-visit statement: confirms 'Artawi-PS1 export pipeline project' by name at 95% completion as of the ministry's Feb 2 inspection -- an independent primary-source confirmation (ministry statement), not a reprint of the MEES piece (MEES ran 4 days later). Verified OK. (3) OilPrice.com (Simon Watkins, original byline, citing the Oil Ministry and an unnamed source close to it, not MEES) -- corroborates the Artawi-PS1 line as ~95% complete, most-advanced piece of TotalEnergies' 4-part Iraq megaproject; url_verifier FAILed the bare 'Ratawi' substring screen (article uses 'Artawi' spelling and doesn't repeat exact figures) but WebFetch read of the live page confirms it is a real, on-topic article discussing this exact pipeline component -- treated as a content false-negative per the verifier's own documented caveat, not excluded. Two related Iraq Business News 2025 articles (Chinese-firm EPSCC contract awards, June/Mar 2025) describe a DIFFERENT, earlier-contracted piece of GGIP -- sour-gas gathering lines from Majnoon/West Qurna-2 to a new gas plant at Artawi -- and were read but NOT used as refs for this crude-export line to avoid conflating the two infrastructure sets.

Capacity intentionally left blank: sources state Ratawi FIELD output is expanding to 100,000 b/d and that this pipeline enables the evacuation of the added volume, but no source states a pipeline-specific nameplate/throughput capacity -- left blank per 'don't invent facts' rather than equating field capacity with pipe capacity. ProposalYear/ProjectLevelCost/FIDStatus left blank -- no source gives a proposal date or cost specific to this line (the $294m/2025 contracts found are for the separate sour-gas gathering scope, not this line). No official GIS route found for the ~30km link; RouteType/RouteAccuracy/RouteNotes filled per route_conventions.md as endpoints-known/low/no-coordinates rather than fabricating geometry. Owner/Parent formatting mirrors the two-tier convention seen on other Iraq JV rows (e.g. P0532 Tuba-Fao: operating-entity % on Owner, full legal-name % on Parent); TotalEnergies, Basra Oil Company, and QatarEnergy all matched to existing GEM entity strings via entity_lookup.py (no new entities needed). Arabic-language search was not attempted this pass (WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-session); the Iraqi Oil Ministry's own reported statement (via Iraq Business News) substitutes as the primary/official-source leg of the >=2-independent-sources bar.

candidates.name: Samawa Refinery–Samawa Power Plant Fuel Oil Pipeline

values.PipelineName: Samawa Refinery–Samawa Power Plant Fuel Oil Pipeline
values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: 6 km point-to-point fuel-oil line between Samawa Refinery and the Samawa Combined-Cycle Power Plant, both sited at Samawa, Al-Muthanna governorate; no official GIS route located, endpoints only (straight-line basis).

candidates.researcher_notes: Two independent, mutually corroborating sources confirm this is a real, completed (not proposed) pipeline: (1) Iraq Business News (English, 2025-04-08) reporting the Oil Pipelines Company brought online a 6 km, 6-inch fuel-oil line from Samawa Refinery to the Samawa Combined-Cycle Power Plant, replacing tanker-truck delivery; (2) qaissqb.com (Arabic, matching the operational date of 7 April 2025 given in-article: 'طول الأنبوب يبلغ 6 كيلومترات وقطره 6 عقدة' -- pipe is 6 km long and 6 inches diameter), naming the same operator (شركة خطوط الأنابيب النفطية / Oil Pipelines Company) and identical route/spec. A third Arabic hit (an Instagram post by samawa.news) cited '5كم' (5 km) but is not an independent written news outlet and is discounted in favor of the two matching 6 km figures from established news sites -- flagging the minor length discrepancy for awareness, not as a blocker. Re-checked against the 86-row existing Iraq roster in discovery_context.json: no row references Muthanna, Samawa, or any refinery-to-power-plant pair in that governorate, confirming this is genuinely missing, not a rename of an existing PID. Add-threshold met: (a) sponsor identified -- Iraq's state Oil Pipelines Company (subsidiary of the Ministry of Oil, per the same owner convention used on the analogous existing rows Ahdeb–Wassit P5292/P5293, Strategic Pipeline-Musaiab P6254, Strategic Pipeline-Al-Khairat P6258); (b) country + concrete endpoints -- Iraq, Samawa Refinery to Samawa Combined-Cycle Power Plant, Al-Muthanna governorate; (c) concrete step -- already operating/completed as of April 2025, the strongest possible status, not a rumor. Entity check: entity_lookup.py found no existing distinct 'Oil Pipelines Company' or 'SCOP' owner entity in the oil tracker (only a generic 'Oil' fuzzy hit), so Owner/Parent were set to 'Iraq Ministry of Oil [100.%]' / 'Ministry of Oil (Iraq) [100.00%]' to match the established convention for this exact class of refinery/pipeline-to-power-plant row rather than minting a new owner string. Route: no GIS/official map found for this short link; RouteAccuracy set to 'low' (endpoints known, straight-line only, both facilities co-located at Samawa). Confidence tier: high -- two independent outlets in two languages, consistent spec and operator, operating status confirmed rather than proposed.
